title: automation: tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer (Helm + Terraform) and upgrade/rollback controls
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments require deterministic tenant bootstrap permissions so installer (Helm) and Terraform modules can create initial tenant resources without interactive operator steps. This PR adds automated RBAC role templates, Terraform IAM bindings, and small installer hooks to support non-interactive tenant onboarding and safe upgrades/rollbacks.

What this PR does:
- Adds namespaced tenant bootstrap ClusterRole/RoleBindings and a minimal ClusterRole for installer automation with least privilege scopes.
- Exposes Helm templates in helm/charts/private-installer for switchable bootstrap modes (interactive | automated).
- Adds Terraform module outputs and IAM binding resources to terraform/modules/private to allow IaC-driven tenant creation during private installs.
- Adds an upgrade/rollback helper script used by the private-installer to preserve RBAC state during in-place upgrades.
- Adds e2e test manifests and a CI job to validate end-to-end tenant bootstrap in a kind cluster.

Checklist:
- [x] Design review (ENG-4271)
- [x] Unit tests for template rendering
- [x] Integration e2e validated in CI (flaky on first run, fixed by idempotency change)
- [x] Docs for operator and terraform usage updated
- [x] Backwards-compatible (no breaking changes to default installer behavior)

Testing and rollout notes: The new Helm switch default is the existing interactive flow. Operators opt-in to automated tenant bootstrap with helm value privateInstaller.bootstrapMode=automated and by providing a bootstrap-secret (service account token) managed by the operator/service account. Terraform users can set module variable enable_rbac_bootstrap=true to wire IAM bindings during terraform apply. CI adds a gated e2e job that runs the full bootstrap flow; initial runs failed due to timing race around CRD readiness and were fixed by adding retry logic in the installer hook.

Security considerations: Templates scoped to namespace where possible; ClusterRole created only to allow installer lifecycle operations (CRD read, tenant CR write) and documented in docs/private/rbac.md. Operators must store bootstrap credentials in KMS-backed secrets.

Rollback behavior: The installer script preserves previous bindings in a stamped configmap and performs a best-effort cleanup on rollback. Rollback is safe by default: if automated bootstrap was used, rollback leaves tenant resources intact but revokes the automation service account after operator confirmation.

release_notes: Adds automated tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer and Terraform modules. Operator can opt-in to automated bootstrap via Helm value privateInstaller.bootstrapMode=automated or Terraform variable enable_rbac_bootstrap=true. Includes installer upgrade/rollback helper and e2e tests to validate idempotency. Non-breaking by default.
notes_for_ops: When enabling automated bootstrap in production, ensure bootstrap service account tokens are provisioned into a KMS-backed secret and rotate after tenant creation. Monitor rbac.bootstrap.errors metric and the new rbac.bootstrap.duration histogram.
regression_risks: Low. Default installer behavior unchanged. Risk comes from operator misconfiguration when enabling automated mode; documented in docs/private/rbac.md.
test_plan: Unit tests for template rendering, CI e2e job that runs kind cluster bootstrap, manual validation on a staging private installer cluster, and terraform apply/destroy cycle checks.
